record.paper_title: Open Problems in Constructive Function Theory
record.original_question: For orthogonal polynomials with varying weights, does the entropy asymptotic formula expressed through the equilibrium measure in the external field remain valid in a more general setting, for example whenever the support of the equilibrium measure is an interval?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 5.6. Is this result valid in a more general setting, say when S_w is an interval?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $w$ be a non-negative weight function on the real line of the form $w(x) = e^{-Q(x)}$, where the external field $Q:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is such that, for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the varying weight $w^{2n}(x) = e^{-2nQ(x)}$ admits associated orthonormal polynomials $\{p_{n,n}\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfying
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}} p_{n,n}(x)\, p_{m,n}(x)\, e^{-2nQ(x)}\,dx = \delta_{n,m}.$$
Associated to $Q$ is the (weighted) equilibrium measure $\mu_w$, i.e. the unique Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ that minimizes the weighted logarithmic energy
$$I_Q(\mu) = \iint \log\frac{1}{|x-y|}\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y) + 2\int Q(x)\,d\mu(x),$$
with compact support $S_w := \operatorname{supp}(\mu_w)$.

Define the (differential) entropy of the squared orthonormal polynomial against the varying weight by
$$E_n(w) := -\int_{\mathbb{R}} p_{n,n}^2(x)\, \log\bigl(p_{n,n}^2(x)\bigr)\, e^{-2nQ(x)}\,dx,$$
and let $E(\mu_w)$ denote the corresponding logarithmic entropy functional of the equilibrium measure $\mu_w$ that, under suitable regularity hypotheses, governs the leading-order asymptotics of $E_n(w)$ as $n\to\infty$.

Under the hypothesis that the asymptotic formula
$$E_n(w) = E(\mu_w) + o(1) \quad (n\to\infty)$$
(expressing the entropy asymptotics of the varying-weight orthogonal polynomials through the equilibrium measure in the external field $Q$) is known to hold in some restricted setting, determine whether the same asymptotic remains valid in the more general setting in which the support $S_w$ of the equilibrium measure is assumed only to be a single interval.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned related work on asymptotics of orthogonal polynomials with varying exponential weights, equilibrium measures in external fields, and entropy estimates (Deift–Kriecherbauer–McLaughlin, Buyarov–Rakhmanov, etc.), but no source explicitly confirms or refutes the extension of the entropy asymptotic formula to the general case where the support of the equilibrium measure is an interval. The current status could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: Entropy function and orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Entropy estimates for orthogonality measures of orthogonal polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature exists on entropy and orthogonal polynomials, but does not directly resolve the interval-support extension.

status_evidence.title: Uniform asymptotics for polynomials orthogonal with respect to varying exponential weights
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotics for orthogonal polynomials with varying exponential weights e^{-nV(x)} via Riemann–Hilbert methods.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background asymptotics framework, but does not address the entropy-asymptotic question with interval support.
